title: Severity axis + --fail-on=<level> CI gate
description:
Today: any finding → exit 1. Real adoption needs severity to be configurable per-check and gated separately from priority (priority sorts the report; severity gates CI).

Acceptance:
- Add Severity enum to cofferdam-core (Info, Low, Medium, High, Critical). Each CheckMeta gets a default_severity; cofferdam.toml can override per-check.
- New CLI flag --fail-on=<info|low|medium|high|critical> (default: medium for now). Exit 1 only when at least one finding ≥ threshold.
- Severity surfaced in text and JSON formatters.
- Defaults: Warning.* = High, Refactor.* = Medium, Design.* = Medium, Readability.* = Low, Consistency.* = Low. Tuned later, fine for v1.
- Compatible with baselines: baselined findings never trigger fail-on regardless of severity.

Design note: priority (computed, sorts) and severity (configured, gates) MUST stay separate axes per the README. Don't collapse them. Severity overrides live in [checks.X.Y] severity = 'high' in cofferdam.toml — depends on cd-4ms landing first.

title: Baseline workflow: cofferdam baseline write/check + --baseline + default fail-on-new
description:
Single biggest adoption unlock. New subcommand 'cofferdam baseline write' snapshots current findings to .cofferdam/baseline.json. 'cofferdam check' auto-detects the baseline file and defaults to --fail-on-new (only NEW findings produce exit code 1; baselined findings still print as 'baselined' but don't fail CI). Override with --no-baseline or --baseline=<path>.

Acceptance:
- Hash key per finding: (relative_path, check_id, rule_signature) where rule_signature is a check-defined stable hash of the matched code (NOT line number — line numbers churn on every reformat). Default rule_signature = SHA-256 of the trimmed offending span text.
- 'cofferdam baseline write' is idempotent and pretty-prints JSON with stable key order so diffs are reviewable.
- Schema versioned: {version: 1, findings: [...]}.
- Smoke test: write baseline on bestefforttools (~396 findings), re-run check, expect exit 0 and 'N findings (all baselined)' summary line.
- Add an unbaselined finding (edit any source file), expect exit 1 and only that finding in the report.
- JSON output gains a 'baselined' boolean per finding so robot consumers can filter.

Design note: rule_signature is the load-bearing decision. Line-number-based baselines invalidate on any reformat and become useless. Span-text-hash works but is fragile to whitespace; trim aggressively. Per-check override of rule_signature lets future checks (e.g. CognitiveComplexity) hash the AST shape rather than text.

Out of scope here: severity gating, --since (separate sub-issues under epic cd-g4y).
close_reason: Implemented baseline write/check workflow. SHA-256-of-trimmed-span signatures; schema versioned at v1; sorted entries; auto-detects .cofferdam/baseline.json; --baseline/--no-baseline/--fail-on-new flags; JSON gets baselined per-finding + summary.new/baselined. Validated end-to-end on bestefforttools (398 findings). Commit d0c9f73.

title: [Epic] Adoption-unlock: baselines, severity gating, --since
description: Without these, every existing TS project fails CI on day-1 of installing cofferdam (default exit-1-on-any-finding × 100s of pre-existing findings). This epic blocks the 'npm install + include in build step' user story. Three sub-issues track baselines (the headline feature), severity gating (escape hatch), and --since <ref> (PR-only mode). Validation target: dropping cofferdam into bestefforttools (325 files, 396 findings) must NOT fail CI on the first run.

title: Stopgap npm wrapper (postinstall binary download)
description:
Phase 4 (cd-napi epic) ships @cofferdam/node via napi-rs prebuilt binaries — that's weeks of work. Meanwhile we want TS users to type `pnpm add -D cofferdam` and have it work TODAY.

Approach: thin npm package whose postinstall hook downloads the matching GitHub Release binary. Pattern used by esbuild (early), wasm-pack, biome (early days), etc.

Steps:
1. Create packages/cofferdam/ with a minimal package.json + scripts/postinstall.js
2. postinstall detects platform/arch (process.platform + process.arch), maps to a release artifact URL, downloads + extracts to node_modules/.bin/cofferdam
3. Bin entry in package.json so `pnpm exec cofferdam` resolves
4. CI: publish to npm on tag push (alongside the existing release.yml)
5. Document in README: `pnpm add -D cofferdam` then `pnpm exec cofferdam check src/`

Phase 4 will replace this with the napi-rs path transparently — same package name, users don't notice. The postinstall approach has known issues (corporate proxies, offline CI, sandboxed npm installs) that the napi-rs prebuilt approach solves; until phase 4 lands, this is the bridge.

Acceptance:
- Tom can `pnpm add -D cofferdam` in rovikore-landing-page and run `pnpm exec cofferdam check src/` without any other setup
- Works on macOS, Linux, Windows (x64 minimum; arm64 if release matrix produces it)
- postinstall failure has a clear error message pointing to the manual install path

title: Distribute cofferdam binary releases (pre-npm)
description:
Cut binary releases NOW so the user can pin cofferdam in their own repos before phase 4's full napi-rs npm publish lands. Enables real-world iteration via dogfooding.

Distribution paths:
1. **GitHub Releases**: tag-triggered, multi-platform binaries from the existing release.yml matrix (Linux x64/arm64 gnu+musl, macOS x64/arm64, Windows x64/arm64). Users `curl | tar` or download. — closest to today's tooling.
2. **cargo install**: `cargo install --git https://github.com/cofferdam/cofferdam cofferdam-cli` — Rust users, works today without any release infra.
3. **homebrew-cofferdam tap**: `brew install cofferdam/tap/cofferdam` — macOS dev experience.
4. **Scoop bucket** (Windows): user already uses scoop heavily.

Phase 4 will replace #1-#3 with the full `@cofferdam/node` npm distribution (the platform-specific binaries via napi-rs prebuilt artifacts). Until then:

Acceptance:
- `v0.0.2` tagged + GH Release published with at minimum linux-x64, mac-arm64, windows-x64 binaries
- Release workflow flips from `if: false` to gated on tag pushes (matches napi-rs template's pattern)
- Install-once instructions in README for each platform
- User can run `cofferdam check` in rovikore-landing-page and one other repo without local clone

Out of scope: npm publish, crates.io publish, Linux distros. Phase 4 / phase 6 territory.

title: Robot mode — AI-first JSON output
description:
Token-economical structured output for AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, aider, etc.).

Flags:
- `--robot` / `--json` — machine-readable output, stable schema, no ANSI, no banner, no totals line
- `--robot --format=toon` — token-optimized format (1.6x more efficient than JSON for repeated keys)
- `--robot-meta` — include cursor + token-budget metadata for paginated runs

Schema (initial draft):
```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "Warning.TripleEquals",
      "category": "warning",
      "priority": 15,
      "severity": "warning",
      "file": "src/foo.ts",
      "line": 42,
      "column": 8,
      "endLine": 42,
      "endColumn": 10,
      "message": "Use === instead of ==",
      "fix": null
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "total": 1, "byCategory": { "warning": 1 }, "durationMs": 183 }
}
```

Why P1: most cofferdam usage will be agent-driven from day one. The text formatter exists for humans; robot mode is the load-bearing surface. Should land before any check work is announced externally.

Acceptance:
- `cofferdam check src/ --robot` produces parseable JSON, exit code matches text mode
- Schema documented + JSON Schema artifact at `schemas/findings.schema.json` for tooling
- Token cost on a 200-finding run ≤ 30% of the text formatter's

title: Cofferdam config file (cofferdam.toml)
description:
Deferred from phase 1 main scope but blocks much of phase 1's usefulness on real codebases. Schema for v0:

[checks."Readability.MaxLineLength"]
limit = 120
severity = "warning"
enabled = true

[checks."Readability.MaxFunctionLength"]
limit = 50

[checks."Design.MaxParameters"]
limit = 5

Discovery:
- Walk up from CWD until cofferdam.toml found, OR git root
- Empty/missing → all defaults
- Per-directory overrides? Defer to phase 3 with severity-axis work

Should land before cd-8 (smoke test) so we can tune the thresholds against real code.
notes: Scope grew per cd-qzv: must include [ignore] section. Globs append to .cofferdamignore patterns at engine level. Precedence: CLI --no-ignore > [ignore].paths > .cofferdamignore > .gitignore > defaults.

title: Wire oxc as the TypeScript parser
description:
Add oxc_parser + oxc_ast as workspace deps in cofferdam-core. Parse SourceFile lazily on first AST access. Decide span shape (oxc::span::Span vs our current Span — likely keep both, with conversion).

Open questions to resolve in the PR:
- Where does the AST live? Owned by SourceFile? CheckContext?
- How do we handle TSX vs TS (parser flag)?
- Error handling: how do we report parse failures? (Probably: emit a Warning.ParseError issue and skip other checks for that file.)

Acceptance:
- oxc parses examples/sample.ts without error
- A new field on CheckContext exposes the AST to checks
- MaxLineLength still works (proves we didn't break the text-only path)
- A parse-error fixture file produces exactly one Warning.ParseError issue, no panics

title: Walk directories + glob in cofferdam check
description:
Replace the phase-0 ad-hoc list of file paths with directory walk + glob support in `cofferdam check`. Default include pattern: `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`. Respect `.gitignore` and `.cofferdamignore` via the `ignore` crate. Single-threaded walk is fine; rayon parallelism comes when oxc lands (cd-3).

Acceptance:
- `cofferdam check` (no args) walks CWD
- `cofferdam check src/` walks the directory
- Files matching .gitignore are skipped
- Output unchanged shape (still grouped by category, priority-sorted)
- Test: walks examples/ and finds the long line in sample.ts

title: Design.LayerViolation — declarative layering rules in cofferdam.toml
description:
Let users declare a layer hierarchy in cofferdam.toml and flag imports that cross it.

EXAMPLE CONFIG:
[layers]
infra  = ["src/infra/**"]
domain = ["src/domain/**"]
app    = ["src/app/**"]

[layers.allow]
domain = ["infra"]                  # domain may import from infra
app    = ["domain", "infra"]        # app may import from both

A 'domain' file importing from 'app' fires a finding. Inverse direction (app → domain) is allowed because 'domain' appears in app's allow list.

Reads imports table built by the graph epic; checks each edge against the declared rules.

Edge cases:
- Files outside any declared layer: configurable (default: ignore).
- Symbolic re-exports through barrel files: walk to the deepest definition's layer.
- Test layer: convention is to allow tests to import from anything; provide a 'test' layer with implicit allow=*.
notes: Child of cd-7h5. The most opinionated of the graph checks; needs the cofferdam.toml options system mature (cd-4ms — already closed).

title: Design.ImportCycle — circular import chains
description:
Flag any cycle in the import graph: A imports B, B imports C, C imports A. Tarjan's SCC over the import graph; emit one finding per cycle with all participating files in 'related' spans.

Configurable max-depth (default unlimited — find all cycles regardless of length). Configurable severity threshold by length (length-2 cycles are usually bugs; length-N≥5 cycles are arch debt).

Type-only imports excluded from cycle detection by default (TS allows type-only cycles cleanly via 'import type'). Configurable.

Output ordering: deterministic — start each cycle from its alphabetically-lowest filename so re-runs produce identical reports.
notes: Child of cd-7h5. Sonnet-friendly once graph lands.

title: Design.OrphanExport — exported but never imported anywhere in project
description:
Flag any export (named, default, type) that no other file imports. Common dead-code source after refactors. Project-wide so single-file checks (tsconfig noUnusedLocals) miss it.

Reads the imports/exports tables built in pass 1 by the graph epic. Emit one finding per orphan export at the export site; no related spans needed.

Edge cases:
- Test files: configurable inclusion (default: skip *_test.ts, *.test.ts, *.spec.ts so test-only exports aren't flagged as orphans).
- Public API entry points: configurable allowlist (default: package.json 'main'/'module'/'exports' targets are NEVER flagged).
- Re-exports through barrel files: the export at the deepest definition is the orphan, not the re-export. Walk the chain.
- Type-only exports: same rule applies; type-only imports count as imports.
notes: Child of cd-7h5 (project graph epic). Sonnet-friendly once cd-7h5 graph infrastructure lands.

title: [epic] Project knowledge graph + graph-aware checks
description:
Build a typed project graph (imports, exports, references, type relations) in pass 1, expose it via CorpusIndex for graph-aware checks in pass 2. The graph is the strategic differentiator versus Credo and ESLint — none of the existing TS linters offer this depth of cross-file reasoning.

DEPENDS ON: cd-d1y (two-pass infrastructure must land first).

GRAPH CONSTRUCTION (pass 1):
- Module resolver (oxc_resolver already a dep) builds an import graph keyed by absolute path.
- Per-file exports table: named exports, default export, re-exports, type-only exports.
- Per-file imports table: source module, imported names, type-only flag.
- Reference index: for each exported symbol, the set of files that import it.

CHILD BEADS (each one sonnet-friendly once the graph exists):
1. Design.OrphanExport — declared, never imported anywhere in the project.
2. Design.ImportCycle — circular import chains (depth N configurable).
3. Design.LayerViolation — declarative layer config in cofferdam.toml; flag imports that cross declared boundaries.
4. Refactor.DeadExport — exported but every consumer marks the import as type-only or never references the symbol after import.
5. Warning.UnusedImport — already common in TS but worth emitting at the project level so single-file checks (like a tsconfig noUnusedLocals) don't miss re-export passthroughs.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS EPIC:
- Type-aware graph (full ts-morph integration) — that's the existing phase 5 work.
- Call graph (function-call resolution) — separate, much harder.
- Cross-file rename safety — IDE/LSP work.

This is the leapfrog over Credo. Credo's two-pass is mostly used for stylistic consistency; the same infrastructure can power genuine architectural analysis when paired with a proper graph.
notes: Created out of cd-d1y design discussion (2026-05-03). Strategic positioning: this is what makes cofferdam not-just-Credo-for-TypeScript.

title: Auto-generated check catalog → VitePress site
description:
Switch the check catalog from a hand-maintained `docs/checks.md` (landed in cd-m3g) to a fully generated artifact set, with a VitePress site as the human-facing renderer. Keep code as the only source of truth — `CheckMeta` plus a per-check companion markdown body — and emit machine-readable artifacts that AI agents will be the primary consumer of.

## Source of truth

- `CheckMeta` in Rust (existing) → metadata: id, category, priority, severity, options, requires_types, consistency, explanation.
- New: per-check companion markdown at `crates/cofferdam-checks/docs/<id>.md`. Loaded into `CheckMeta` via `body: &'static str = include_str!("../docs/<id>.md")`.
  - Body is the long-form prose: motivation, bad/good examples, deliberate non-flagged shapes, related checks.
  - Build-script (or doc-test) assertion: every entry in `all_builtins()` has a companion file present; failing companion = compile error.
  - Seed content from `docs/checks.md` (cd-m3g) — split into per-check files in the same commit that wires the include_str!.

## Generated artifacts

One subcommand, multiple outputs, all from the same iteration over `all_builtins()`:

```
cofferdam gen-docs --out=docs/
```

Emits:

1. **`docs/checks.json`** — schema-stable index. Array of `{ id, category, priority, severity, options, requires_types, consistency, explanation, body, examples_url }`. Hosted at a stable URL (e.g. `https://cofferdam.dev/checks.json`). The canonical machine artifact for agents.
2. **`docs/checks/<id>.md`** — one file per check, with frontmatter (`id`, `category`, `priority`, `severity`, `options`) plus the body text. Consumed by VitePress.
3. **`docs/checks/index.md`** — generated landing page grouped by category, links to each check.
4. **`docs/llms.txt`** — root index in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format. Curated entry points: install snippet, catalog index URL, JSON URL, key CLI flags.

CI gate: `cofferdam gen-docs --check` re-runs the generator against the committed `docs/` and fails if anything would change. Same shape as `cargo fmt --check`.

## Website (VitePress)

- New directory: `website/` (or `docs-site/` — bikeshed at implementation).
- VitePress consumes `docs/checks/*.md` directly. Sidebar auto-generated from category frontmatter. Local search enabled (no Algolia).
- Default theme; minimal customisation. The site is a renderer, not a brand surface.
- Deploy via GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages (cofferdam.github.io/cofferdam) or to Vercel under a chosen domain. Decide at implementation time — both are CI-friendly.
- Versioning: out of scope for v1. Path-based versioning (`/v0.1/checks/...`) once we hit 1.0.

## Why VitePress

Picked over Astro Starlight, Docusaurus, mdBook because the catalog is a pure docs site (no marketing landing page, no interactive components today), VitePress is purpose-built for that use case with the lowest config-to-result ratio, and Vite-fast incremental builds matter when `cofferdam gen-docs` re-runs on every check change.

If we ever need interactive components (e.g. wasm "try cofferdam in your browser"), revisit and migrate to Astro Starlight — both produce static HTML, so the agent-readability story is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- `crates/cofferdam-checks/docs/<id>.md` exists for every entry in `all_builtins()`. Build fails (or `cargo test` fails) if a companion is missing.
- `cofferdam gen-docs --out=docs/` produces `checks.json`, `checks/<id>.md` per check, `checks/index.md`, `llms.txt`. Idempotent: running twice in a row produces no diff.
- CI workflow runs `cofferdam gen-docs --check` and fails on drift.
- VitePress site builds successfully, serves the catalog at a stable URL, has working local search and a sitemap.
- `docs/checks.md` (the hand-written cd-m3g page) is replaced by the generated `docs/checks/index.md` — same anchors and content, no broken inbound links.
- `cofferdam explain <id>` keeps working (already sources from `CheckMeta`); the long-form `body` becomes available via a future `--full` flag (separate bead).

## Out of scope (separate beads)

- `cofferdam explain --full` flag rendering the markdown body (cd-brp follow-up).
- Versioning of the published site.
- Marketing landing page on the same domain.
- Custom theme work beyond the VitePress default.

title: Consistency.QuoteStyle
description: Already named in the README phased roadmap as the phase-2 canary. Two-pass mode: scan every string literal, pick the dominant quote style as the project default, emit findings for non-conforming strings. Depends on engine two-pass support (separate prereq bead). One file in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/consistency.rs (new module if it doesn't exist), one fixture in examples/, one registration in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/lib.rs::all_builtins().

title: Engine: two-pass mode for consistency checks
description:
Add a generalized two-pass mode to the engine: pass 1 collects evidence, pass 2 emits findings against the collected baseline. Canary check: Consistency.QuoteStyle.

The infrastructure reuses the existing CorpusIndex slot pattern (already used by Design.DuplicateExportName, Refactor.DuplicateBlock) but adds an explicit pass-2 hook on the Check trait — finalize-style — so consistency checks can declare 'I need to see all files before emitting'.

Scope:
- Engine pass-2 hook on Check trait (sibling to finalize, but per-file rather than corpus-wide).
- Pass-1 evidence storage via existing CorpusIndex.
- Consistency.QuoteStyle as the canary: count single vs double quotes per file, emit findings against the dominant style.
- Threshold for 'dominant' = strict majority (>50%); per-file scope (not project-wide). Both decisions can be revisited via OptionSpec later.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — handled by separate epic 'Project knowledge graph':
- Project-wide imports/exports/references graph.
- Graph-aware checks (orphan exports, cycles, layering, dead code).
- Cross-file rename safety.

Two-pass infra is a prereq for the graph epic but the graph design is not bundled here. Keep the pass-2 hook generic enough that a future graph builder (running in pass 1) can expose its results via the same CorpusIndex pattern.

title: Refactor.PreferOptionalChain + Refactor.PreferNullishCoalescing
description: Modern TS idioms. Type-aware tier (phase 5) is the right home for full coverage, but high-confidence cases (e.g. a && a.b && a.b.c) are detectable from AST shape alone — ship now, expand in phase 5. Additions to crates/cofferdam-checks/src/refactor.rs (alongside CyclomaticComplexity / CognitiveComplexity / DuplicateBlock). Mark requires_types: false initially; flip to true when the type-aware tier lands and the rules grow to cover ambiguous cases. Two checks, one bead.
close_reason: Implemented Refactor.PreferOptionalChain (priority 5, severity Low) — flags 'lhs && lhs.b' patterns where LHS is a pure reference chain and RHS extends LHS by exactly one .step / [step] / .step(). Refactor.PreferNullishCoalescing (priority 3, severity Low) — flags 'member-access || default-literal' where default is string/num/bool/null/undefined/array/object literal. Two fixtures with comprehensive flagged + non-flagged cases. Real-repo validation: bestefforttools surfaces 2 PreferOptionalChain (genuine 3-step && chains) + 34 PreferNullishCoalescing (genuine '|| string-default' / '|| 0' patterns), zero false positives spot-checked. 214 tests pass, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Warning pack: NoConsoleLog + NoDebugger + NoEval
description: Three AST-only single-node visitor checks following the existing Warning.TripleEquals recipe in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/warning.rs. (1) NoConsoleLog: match CallExpression where callee is MemberExpression{object:Identifier('console'),property:Identifier(_)}. Default Low severity, base_priority -10. (2) NoDebugger: match DebuggerStatement (even simpler). (3) NoEval: match CallExpression where callee is Identifier('eval') OR MemberExpression{object:Identifier('Function'),property:Identifier('prototype')}. Default High severity (universal security ban). One fixture per check in examples/. Register all three in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/lib.rs::all_builtins(). Parallel-safe: each check is its own struct — can fan out via subagents per CLAUDE.md dispatch rules. Three checks, one bead.
close_reason: Implemented Warning.NoConsoleLog (any console.X call, base_priority -10, severity Low), Warning.NoDebugger (DebuggerStatement, priority 10, Medium), and Warning.NoEval (eval() and new Function(), priority 18, High). Three fixtures in examples/. Real-repo validation: bestefforttools surfaces 75 genuine console calls + 0 debugger + 0 eval, zero false positives spot-checked. 214 tests pass, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Autofix capability + Warning.TripleEquals POC (== → ===)
description: Phase-4 in the README roadmap, but a single autofix as proof-of-concept dramatically changes how the tool feels. Pick TripleEquals because it's the simplest mechanical replacement. Adds Cmd::Fix subcommand in crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs. Adds an autofix capability to the Check trait in crates/cofferdam-core/src/check.rs (e.g., fn autofix(&self, issue: &Issue, source: &SourceFile) -> Option<TextEdit>). Implementation in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/warning.rs::TripleEquals — already has byte spans of == / != operators, just emit === / !== over them. Apply edits in order; write the file atomically (temp + rename). NOT parallel-safe — touches the central Check trait. Out of scope: --interactive, conflict resolution between checks editing the same span.

title: CLI ergonomics: --max-issues=N, --quiet, NO_COLOR
description: Table-stakes CLI flags. All in crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs. --max-issues=N: short-circuit Engine::analyze once N findings collected, bounds output for huge repos and CI memory. --quiet: suppress info lines, only emit findings (pairs naturally with --max-issues). NO_COLOR env: industry-standard. Verify whether crates/cofferdam-formatters/src/text.rs already honors it via owo-colors' OwoColorize::if_supports_color (auto-detects NO_COLOR).
close_reason: Implemented --max-issues=N (top-N truncation, gate uses full set, JSON adds optional truncated_from), --quiet (suppresses info eprintlns + trailing summary + no-findings line), and verified NO_COLOR (text formatter emits no ANSI; documented). 6 new tests, build/clippy/fmt clean, smoke-tested against bestefforttools.

title: cofferdam check --watch (re-run on file save)
description: Single biggest inner-loop DX improvement before LSP lands in phase 6. ~50 LOC using the notify crate (add to crates/cofferdam-cli/Cargo.toml). Wrap the existing Engine::analyze call in crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs::Cmd::Check handler with a debounced loop. Honor .gitignore / .cofferdamignore for the watch set (re-use crates/cofferdam-engine/src/discover.rs).
close_reason: Won't do; LSP supersedes. The LSP server (phase 6) is where 're-run on edit' belongs — IDE handles file scoping, debouncing, error-list rendering. CLI watch would awkwardly recreate that in a terminal. Cofferdam runs in ~270ms on 325 files; up-arrow + Enter beats engineering a watch loop. Cross-platform watching (Docker bind mounts, NFS, symlinks, WSL2) is an edge-case minefield with low-ROI for the minority of terminal-only users. Reopen if a real user files an issue.

title: cofferdam check --explain <check_id>
description: Print the check's full doc + good/bad example. Today users hit a finding and have no in-tool path to 'why is this flagged?'. CheckMeta::explanation already exists in crates/cofferdam-core/src/check.rs — just needs surfacing. New CLI subcommand or flag in crates/cofferdam-cli/src/main.rs around the Cli/Cmd enums (line 26-62 area). After cd-b3k lands the generated catalog at docs/checks/<category>.md, --explain can cat the relevant section; until then, fall back to CheckMeta::explanation raw.
close_reason: Implemented 'cofferdam explain <check_id>' subcommand. Prints CheckMeta (category, default severity, base priority, type-aware/consistency flags, options, explanation) in human text or --robot JSON. Unknown ID prints substring suggestions or full list with exit 2. 5 unit tests in crates/cofferdam-cli/src/explain.rs.

title: [Epic] Post-v1 next ring
description: Improvements that compound the value of cofferdam once the cd-g4y adoption-unlock epic ships. Sourced from .claude/plans/post-v1-roadmap.md (drafted 2026-05-03). Covers: Bucket 1 (CLI ergonomics: explain/watch/max-issues/autofix POC), Bucket 3 (check pack expansion + engine two-pass for QuoteStyle), Bucket 4 (community hygiene — issues + proposals only, no PRs accepted), Bucket 7 (test rigor). Buckets 2 (distribution beyond npm), 5 (perf+observability), and 6 (VS Code extension) deferred. Filing now because cd-g4y is materially underway (3 of 11 children closed).

title: [v1] .cofferdamignore — promote from 'wired but invisible' to a documented v1 feature
description:
The wiring already exists ('discover.rs:76' uses the ignore crate's 'add_custom_ignore_filename(".cofferdamignore")', so full gitignore-syntax including negation works today). What's missing for v1 is everything around it: discovery, scaffolding, documentation, config interaction, and the policy on what to ignore vs baseline vs cache.

Acceptance:

1. Documentation
   - Dedicated page 'docs/configuration/ignoring-files.md' (under VitePress site, cd-t6n) covering: gitignore-syntax (incl. negation with !), precedence vs .gitignore, vs CLI '--no-ignore', vs per-check 'exclude' globs in cofferdam.toml. Worked examples: ignore vendored dirs, ignore generated *.gen.ts, un-ignore a single file inside an ignored dir.
   - npm README (cd-dh4) gains a 4-line snippet showing creating a '.cofferdamignore' to scope past 'dist/'.
   - 'cofferdam check --help' line for '--no-ignore' updated to mention both filenames + link.

2. First-run scaffolding ('cofferdam init', cd-fnm)
   - 'init' writes a starter '.cofferdamignore' with commented-out common entries: 'node_modules/', 'dist/', 'build/', 'coverage/', '*.generated.ts', '*.gen.ts', '__generated__/', 'storybook-static/'. Commented so users opt-in line-by-line and see what would be plausibly ignored — not a wall of muted lines.
   - If '.cofferdamignore' already exists: 'init' leaves it alone (never overwrites).

3. Diagnostics ('cofferdam doctor', cd-oa3)
   - Doctor reports: '.cofferdamignore present at <path>', and the count of files it excludes from the default scope ('N files in src/ ignored by .cofferdamignore'). High-value signal — users frequently misconfigure this and don't notice until findings disappear.

4. Config interaction ('cofferdam.toml', cd-4ms)
   - cd-4ms acceptance grows an '[ignore]' section: '[ignore] paths = ["foo/**", "!foo/keep.ts"]'. Globs append to '.cofferdamignore' patterns at engine level (not file-merged on disk). Documented precedence: CLI '--no-ignore' > '[ignore].paths' in TOML > '.cofferdamignore' > '.gitignore' > defaults.
   - File this scope-bump as a comment/note on cd-4ms; do NOT file a separate bead (one config file, one loader bead).

5. Baseline / cache placement policy (resolves the gap in cd-fnm and cd-d31)
   - Canonical layout: '.cofferdam/baseline.json' (committed) and '.cofferdam/cache/' (gitignored). 'cofferdam init' writes '.gitignore' entries for '.cofferdam/cache/' specifically, NOT the whole '.cofferdam/' directory.
   - '.cofferdamignore' itself is a regular project file: committed, NOT in any ignore list.
   - Documented in 'docs/configuration/baselines.md' and 'docs/configuration/ignoring-files.md'.

6. Verification
   - Smoke test: bestefforttools with no '.cofferdamignore' → N findings; add '.cofferdamignore' with 'app/components/legacy/**' → N - K findings, K matching the legacy-dir count. Asserts engine respects the file end-to-end (already does, but lock the contract with a test).
   - Test: negation pattern works (ignore 'vendor/**' but un-ignore 'vendor/keep.ts').
   - Test: '--no-ignore' flag bypasses both '.gitignore' AND '.cofferdamignore' (matches the help text).

- cd-4ms (extend with [ignore] section)
- cd-fnm (init seeds starter file + .gitignore policy)
- cd-oa3 (doctor surfaces ignore state)
- cd-t6n / cd-b3k (docs site page)

'.cofferdamignore' is the broad-stroke 'pretend these files don't exist' lever; per-check scoping is the surgical lever. Both ship; they don't compete.

title: [CI] cofferdam-check GitHub composite Action
description:
The diagram's CI/BUILD STEP quadrant currently demands users hand-roll a workflow with pnpm setup + cofferdam invocation. A composite Action collapses that to one 'uses:' block — the standard pattern for any CLI that wants to live in CI. This is the single biggest UX win for the build-step story without waiting for SARIF/phase-6.

Acceptance:
- New repo (or path under this repo): 'TAJD/cofferdam-action' as a public composite GitHub Action. If a separate repo, mirror tags from cofferdam (v0.1.4 → cofferdam-action@v0.1.4 + a moving v1 tag).
- 'action.yml' inputs: paths (default 'src/'), since (default ''), fail-on (default 'medium'), baseline (default '.cofferdam/baseline.json'), version (default 'latest'), config (default 'cofferdam.toml').
- Steps: download the matching cofferdam binary from GitHub Releases (no npm install — composite Action should be standalone, not require Node). Use the platform of the runner. Cache by version key.
- Run cofferdam check with the resolved flags. Capture JSON output.
- Translate findings to GitHub workflow commands ('::error file=...,line=...,col=...,title=<check_id>::<message>') so devs see red squiggles on the PR diff WITHOUT SARIF wiring. This is the v1 substitute for cd-x6? (SARIF, phase 6).
- Exit with the binary's exit code so the job goes red on findings ≥ fail-on.
- README example: 5-line workflow that any TS repo can paste.
- Smoke test in this repo: a workflow that uses the action against examples/ and asserts annotations are emitted.

Depends on cd-d31 (--baseline), cd-3pn (--since), cd-t1a (--fail-on) — all flags the action wraps.

Design note: composite Action over JS Action because we don't want to ship a Node runtime when the cofferdam binary is the actual workload. Composite means each step is shell + the binary; smaller surface, easier to audit.

title: [Docs site] Generated CLI reference + check catalog (drift-proof via CI)
description:
Generate two doc surfaces from the source of truth so they cannot drift: the CLI reference (from clap) and the per-check catalog (from CheckMeta). If hand-written, both go stale within weeks.

Acceptance:
- New subcommand 'cofferdam docs export --out <dir>'. Walks all_builtins() and writes one Markdown file per category to <dir>/checks/{consistency,design,readability,refactor,warning}.md. Each entry: id, default severity, default priority, explanation (from CheckMeta), default options (if any), one good/bad example pulled from examples/<fixture>.ts (so the example is the same file the test suite exercises).
- Same subcommand also writes <dir>/reference/cli.md by recursing the clap Command tree (use the 'clap-markdown' crate, ~5-line integration; or hand-roll if it doesn't render the way we want).
- Closes the implementation side of cd-m3g (check catalog) and cd-l32 (output formats — that one becomes a hand-written reference page that the generator does NOT touch, since it's prose, not enum-derived).
- New CI step in ci.yml after build/test: run 'cofferdam docs export --out docs/' and fail if 'git diff --exit-code docs/checks docs/reference/cli.md' is non-empty. This is the structural guarantee against drift.
- Local workflow: contributors run the export themselves before pushing if they edited a check or a flag. Document this in CONTRIBUTING.md (and create CONTRIBUTING.md if missing — keep it small).

Depends on cd-g4y umbrella; coordinates with cd-m3g (which becomes 'curate the prose intro at the top of each generated category file' rather than 'write all 5 files by hand').

Design note: generated content lives between explicit '<!-- BEGIN GENERATED -->' / '<!-- END GENERATED -->' markers in each file so the human-written intro at the top of each category page survives regeneration. The export command rewrites only between those markers.

title: End-to-end npm install smoke test in CI
description:
The user-facing install story is 'npm install -D cofferdam && npx cofferdam check src/'. Nothing in CI verifies this works on a clean machine for every release.

Acceptance:
- New CI job in .github/workflows/ (or extend release.yml post-publish): on a fresh ubuntu-latest + macos-latest + windows-latest matrix:
  1. mkdir tmp && cd tmp && npm init -y
  2. npm install -D cofferdam@<just-published-version>
  3. Verify node_modules/cofferdam/bin/cofferdam(.exe) exists post-postinstall
  4. Write a 3-line tsconfig + a 5-line src/index.ts with a known finding (== usage)
  5. npx cofferdam check src/ --robot, parse JSON, assert exit 1 and findings[0].check_id == 'Warning.TripleEquals'
  6. Test --ignore-scripts path: re-install with --ignore-scripts, expect the bin/cofferdam.js shim to print the manual-install instructions and exit 1
- Runs on each tag push AFTER publish-npm completes, gated on success.
- Failures must page: whoever cuts releases needs to know within minutes if the install path broke.

Design note: smoke separately from build/release jobs so a flaky network on npm install doesn't roll back an otherwise good release. Use 'needs: publish-npm' so the package is actually fetchable.

title: Inline suppression directives: // cofferdam-disable-next-line
description:
Even with config + baselines, devs need an inline escape hatch for individual false positives. Industry-standard syntax (matches eslint, biome).

Acceptance:
- Comment forms supported:
  - '// cofferdam-disable-next-line' — suppress all checks on the next non-blank line
  - '// cofferdam-disable-next-line Warning.TripleEquals' — suppress one check
  - '// cofferdam-disable-next-line Warning.TripleEquals, Design.MaxParameters' — suppress multiple
  - '/* cofferdam-disable */ ... /* cofferdam-enable */' — block suppression
- Implemented in cofferdam-engine post-collection: read leading comments per file, build a suppression map keyed by (line, check_id), filter the issue stream before sort.
- Suppressed findings disappear from text output but appear in JSON output with a 'suppressed' boolean (so robot consumers and dashboards can still see them).
- Unknown check IDs in the directive log a Consistency.UnknownSuppression finding (don't silently swallow typos).
- Documented in docs/suppression.md (closes the docs side of cd-zaf).

Design note: filter post-collection (not pre-check) so the same suppression code path works for every check without each check having to opt in. Cost: visitors run on suppressed regions. Cheap — these directives are rare.

Out of scope: file-level disable headers (separate later if needed).

title: PR-only mode: --since <git-ref>
description:
Run cofferdam only on files changed vs a base branch. Complements baselines for the PR-CI use case where 'changed files only' is faster and clearer than 'new findings only'.

Acceptance:
- New flag --since=<ref> (e.g. --since=main, --since=origin/main, --since=HEAD~5).
- Resolution via 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AMR <ref>...HEAD' (three-dot to use merge-base).
- Restricts the discovery set to those files; everything else in the engine is unchanged.

- Errors loudly if not in a git repo or ref doesn't resolve.
- Smoke test: bestefforttools — 'cofferdam check --since HEAD~1' touches only files changed in the last commit.

Design note: git invocation via std::process::Command — don't pull libgit2/git2 just for this; libgit2 doubles binary size. Trade-off accepted: requires git on PATH at run time, which is true of every CI environment.

title: Add Refactor.DuplicateBlock (DRY) check
description: New check: detect near-identical statement blocks across files in a single cofferdam run. Likely approach: token/AST hashing of statement runs above a minimum size (>= N tokens OR >= M statements), bucket-and-compare to find duplicates, emit one Issue per duplicate set referencing all locations. Open design questions (resolve in a child design doc before implementation): (1) hash granularity — raw tokens vs. canonicalised AST (rename-resilient)? (2) cross-file engine API — does CheckContext expose a corpus, or do we need an aggregator pass? (3) thresholds + how to surface the N>2 case in the Issue model. Plan first, then implement.
design:
## Decisions

- Detection modes: AST canonicalised hashing (default ON) + token-stream hashing (opt-in flag include_tokens).
- Engine integration: aggregator pattern via the typed shared-corpus API delivered by cd-0ps.
- Issue model: one issue per duplicate set. Uses Issue.related: Vec<Span> (delivered by cd-0ps).
- Defaults: min_statements = 6, min_tokens = 50 (used by token mode), include_tokens = false, include_ast = true. All four configurable via cofferdam.toml once cd-4ms lands; for now, hardcoded with constructor args.
- Canonicalisation: identifier names replaced with per-block locals ($0, $1 ...); literals KEPT literal-sensitive at v1 (=== 5 not equal === 6) to avoid noise. Revisit after bestefforttools validation.

## Cross-file API (delivered by cd-0ps)

cd-0ps lands a typed-key shared corpus. DuplicateBlock uses it like:

    pub static DUPLICATE_FINGERPRINTS: CorpusKey<Vec<Fingerprint>> =
        CorpusKey::new("Refactor.DuplicateBlock.fingerprints");

    impl Check for DuplicateBlock {
        fn run(&self, file, ctx) -> Vec<Issue> {
            ctx.corpus.with_slot(&DUPLICATE_FINGERPRINTS, |fps| {
                fps.extend(self.fingerprints_for(file));
            });
            Vec::new()
        }
        fn finalize(&self, ctx) -> Vec<Issue> {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            ctx.corpus.with_slot(&DUPLICATE_FINGERPRINTS, |fps| {
                out = aggregate_duplicates(fps);
            });
            out
        }
    }

A Fingerprint is { hash: u64, kind: AstHash | TokenHash, file_id: u32, span: Span }. Two checks could share a slot by reusing the same CorpusKey; DuplicateBlock owns its own slot.

## Implementation steps

### Step 1 — cd-0ps engine prerequisite (separate issue)

Delivers: corpus module, CorpusKey<T>, CorpusIndex, CheckContext.corpus, FinalizeContext, breaking finalize signature, Issue.related, formatter wiring. Single-agent, blocks this issue.

### Step 2 — DuplicateBlock skeleton

Replace any stub in crates/cofferdam-checks/src/refactor.rs. Struct holds the four config fields. META: id Refactor.DuplicateBlock, category Refactor, base_priority 12, options listing min_statements / min_tokens / include_tokens / include_ast.

Define DUPLICATE_FINGERPRINTS as a module-level CorpusKey constant.

### Step 3 — AST mode (default on)

In Check::run when include_ast:

- Visit Program, walk every BlockStatement and Program body.
- Slide a window of min_statements consecutive Statement nodes.
- Canonicalise: walk the subtree; map each IdentifierReference / BindingIdentifier / IdentifierName to a stable index based on first occurrence within the window. Keep literal values verbatim. Drop spans/comments from the hash input.
- Hash with twox-hash::Xxh3 (or std DefaultHasher to start; perf-tune later).
- Push Fingerprint { hash, kind: AstHash, file_id, span } into the corpus slot via ctx.corpus.with_slot.

Check::run returns empty.

### Step 4 — Token mode (opt-in)

Only runs when include_tokens. Slide an N-token window over the file lexer output, canonicalise identifiers to id and literals to lit, hash, push as kind: TokenHash.

### Step 5 — finalize() implementation

- ctx.corpus.with_slot(&DUPLICATE_FINGERPRINTS, |fps| ...).
- Group by hash.
- For each group with len >= 2: sort spans by (file_path, start_byte); pick first as primary; rest become Issue.related; emit one Issue per group.
- Dedupe overlapping spans across modes (an AST-mode hit and a token-mode hit covering the same byte range collapse into the AST one).

### Step 6 — Fixtures

- examples/duplicate_block.ts: two functions with structurally-identical bodies but different param + local names should flag. One distinct function should NOT flag. One short helper under min_statements should NOT flag.
- examples/duplicate_block_tokens.ts: repeated multi-line expression that AST mode misses because it spans non-statement boundaries should flag ONLY with include_tokens.

### Step 7 — Verification

Per CLAUDE.md verification block: cargo build/test/clippy/fmt + cargo run on the fixture. After implementation, run on C:/Users/tajdi/bestefforttools and capture the top 10 findings before handing off to cd-3ax.

## Sub-issues (file once cd-0ps lands)

- cd-qnu.2 — AST-mode DuplicateBlock + finalize aggregation. Uses cd-0ps API.
- cd-qnu.3 — Token-mode opt-in path. Depends on cd-qnu.2.
- cd-qnu.4 — Config wiring once cofferdam.toml (cd-4ms) exists. Depends on cd-qnu.2 + cd-4ms.

title: Robot mode — compact line-delim format
description:
JSON output (cd-yvm) is functional but 1.85x text mode bytes due to repeated field names per finding (366 findings × full schema = bloat). For real token economy, ship a one-finding-per-line pipe-delimited format alongside JSON.

Proposed: `--format=compact` emits a single header line + one record per finding:

```
priority|severity|category|id|file|line|column|message
-5|warning|readability|Readability.MaxLineLength|examples/sample.ts|8|121|line is 149 characters, exceeds limit of 120
```

- Stable header — parsers split on pipe
- Messages with literal pipes get backslash-escaped
- Well-formed even when zero findings (header only)

Inspired by cass's `--robot-format compact` pattern. JSON stays the canonical machine format; compact is the agent-shoveling-context-into-prompt format.

Acceptance:
- 200-finding run produces output ≤ 35% of text formatter's bytes (and ≤ 50% of JSON)
- Header documented at `docs/output-formats.md`
- `--robot --format=compact` is a valid combo

title: Refactor.UnusedVariable AST check
description:
Local-binding scope only — no cross-file analysis (that's phase 5 / type-aware).

Edge cases:
- Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` — flag each unused binding individually
- Rest patterns: `const [a, ...rest] = arr` — rest is always considered used (intentional)
- Underscore prefix: `_unused` is conventionally suppressed — don't flag
- Function parameters: flag unused params (with same _-prefix exception)
- Catch parameters: `catch (e)` where e is unused — flag

Out of scope (defer to cd-9 / phase 5):
- Imports (handled by tree-shaker, not here)
- Class fields (need type info to be precise)

- Fixture covering each edge case above
- base_priority: 10 (Refactor)
close_reason: Implemented Refactor.UnusedVariable (priority 10, severity Low) using oxc_semantic for proper scope/reference tracking. Filters: type-only symbols (TypeAlias/Interface/Enum/TypeParameter/TypeImport/Import/etc.) skipped per bead; underscore prefix opts out; rest patterns ([...rest], ...args) skipped; TS function-signature parameter names (TSFunctionType, TSMethodSignature, TSCallSignature, TSConstructSignature, TSIndexSignature) skipped — they're documentation, not bindings; named function/class expressions skipped (React.forwardRef pattern). Module-scope bindings skipped in v1 (might be exported; we don't walk the export AST yet). Real-repo validation: 0 false positives on bestefforttools (after the TS-signature + named-expr filters), 4 genuine hits on gistreact. 11-case fixture covering let/const/var, _-prefix, destructuring (each binding independent), array/param rest, function params, catch params, nested scopes, module scope. 221 tests pass, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Warning.UnusedImport — project-aware unused-import detection
description:
Project-level unused-import check that catches the cases tsconfig noUnusedLocals misses, specifically re-export passthroughs:

  // foo.ts
  export { Bar } from './bar';   // 'Bar' counted as 'used' by noUnusedLocals
                                 // but if no one imports Bar from foo.ts, this is dead.

By reading the project graph, we can confirm whether the re-exported symbol has any downstream consumer. If not, flag at the re-export site.

For non-re-export single-file cases (a plain unused import), defer to tsc/eslint — they already do it well at the file level. Cofferdam's value-add is the cross-file projection.

Configurable: project-aware mode (graph) vs file-only mode (defer to tsc).

EDGE CASES:
- Side-effect imports (// import './polyfill';) — never flag.
- Type-only re-exports — same logic, just type-aware.
- Default export re-naming chains.
notes: Child of cd-7h5. P3 — overlap with tsc/eslint means lower marginal value than OrphanExport.

title: Refactor.DeadExport — exported, imported, but never referenced
description:
Stricter than OrphanExport: exports that ARE imported but every consumer either marks the import as type-only-and-never-actually-uses-the-type, OR imports the symbol and never references it after import.

This is the post-refactor 'someone removed the use site but left the import + export' case. Quieter than OrphanExport (genuinely never imported) but more common in active codebases.

Requires the graph epic's per-file usage analysis: for each imported symbol, count references in the importing file's AST. Zero references = dead from that consumer; if all consumers are dead, the export itself is dead.

Lower priority than OrphanExport because false-positive risk is higher (e.g., dynamic imports via string keys, decorator-injected references).
notes: Child of cd-7h5. P3 because false-positive surface is wider; ship after OrphanExport (cd-?) lands and we have user feedback.

title: [Onboarding] cofferdam doctor — diagnose install/config issues
description:
When a user's cofferdam install or configuration is broken, today they see a low-level error and have to figure it out themselves. 'cofferdam doctor' is the standard escape hatch for this class of problem (precedent: bd doctor, npm doctor, brew doctor). Critical when the install path crosses npm postinstall + prebuilt binary download + custom config — the failure surface is wide and the error messages are scattered.

Acceptance:
- New subcommand 'cofferdam doctor' (no required args). Runs a series of named checks and reports each as ✓ / ⚠ / ✗ with a one-line remediation hint on failure. Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail.
- Checks at minimum:
  1. Binary integrity: self-version matches expected, executable bit set (unix), runs without crashing
  2. Config: cofferdam.toml exists? If yes, parses cleanly? Unknown keys flagged as warnings.
  3. Baseline: .cofferdam/baseline.json exists? If yes, schema version matches? Findings reference still-existing files?
  4. Git: in a git repo (so --since works)? git binary on PATH?
  5. Discovery: at least one .ts/.tsx file under default scope, OR an explicit scope override in config?
  6. Suppression directives: any unknown check IDs referenced in source comments? (Re-uses the directive parser from cd-5t7.)
  7. (npm install only) bin/cofferdam(.exe) is the same version as the wrapper expects.
- '--robot' / JSON output: structured per-check result for consumers (the GitHub Action wraps doctor as a pre-flight).
- Documented in docs/getting-started/ and linked from any error message that doctor would have caught.

Design note: doctor is a diagnostic tool, not a fixer. It must NEVER auto-modify files (no auto-write of cofferdam.toml, no auto-rebaseline). Show the user what's wrong; let them decide. Fixers are 'cofferdam init' (config) and 'cofferdam baseline write' (baseline).

title: [Release hygiene] CHANGELOG.md + Keep-a-Changelog gate in release.yml
description:
release.yml's 'generate_release_notes: true' produces GitHub Release notes but the repo has no CHANGELOG.md. For a tool that gates CI, downstream users pinning '^0.1.x' or '~0.1.x' need a single canonical source for 'what changed in this version' that doesn't require navigating GitHub Releases. Standard for any npm package consumed in build pipelines.

Acceptance:
- 'CHANGELOG.md' at repo root following Keep-a-Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) format. Headings: ## [Unreleased], ## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD, with subheadings Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security.
- Backfill entries for v0.1.1 through current shipped version from git log (one-shot effort, ~30 min).
- New release.yml step before publish: assert that the [Unreleased] section is empty AND a [<tag-version>] section exists matching the tag. Fail the release if not. Forces every release to ship a changelog entry.
- 'CHANGELOG.md' added to packages/cofferdam/'files' array so it ships in the npm tarball (npmjs.com renders it on a 'Versions' tab).
- Document the workflow in CONTRIBUTING.md: 'add to [Unreleased], move to a versioned section as part of the release commit'.
- Linked from docs/about/ and the npm README.

Design note: don't auto-generate from commits. Conventional-commits-to-changelog tools turn commit messages into noise; a hand-curated CHANGELOG is short, useful, and forces 'is this change worth telling users about?' as a discipline.

title: Refactor.CognitiveComplexity — mixed-operator rule (Sonar B3)
description: Today every &&/||/?? counts as +1. Sonar B3: a SEQUENCE of same-kind operators counts as +1 total; switching kind adds +1. So 'a && b && c' is +1 (one && sequence), but 'a && b || c' is +2 (one && segment + one || segment). Implementation: when entering a LogicalExpression that is itself the child of another LogicalExpression with the same operator, do NOT add — only the outermost (or kind-changing) one counts. Track parent-operator context via a stack. Fixture: a chain of && (score +1), a chain of || (+1), a mixed && and || (+2).

title: Refactor.CognitiveComplexity — plain-else cost (Sonar B2)
description: Currently the visitor walks else-if chains correctly (no extra nesting penalty for sibling ifs) but ignores plain else blocks entirely. Sonar B2 says: plain 'else' adds +1 flat (no nesting penalty). Implementation: in visit_if_statement, when alternate is non-IfStatement, call self.flat() once before walking the alternate body. Add fixture exercising plain-else and verify the score increases by exactly 1 per else.
close_reason: Merged in HEAD. CogVisitor now handles plain-else (+1 flat), recursion (+1 per direct self-call), and mixed-operator sequences (+1 per kind segment). Three fixtures + 148 tests pass. bestefforttools regression-clean at 396 findings (B2+B4 score increases offset B3 decreases). Three subagents dispatched in parallel landed cleanly with zero merge conflicts.

title: Refactor.CognitiveComplexity — recursion penalty (Sonar B4)
description: Sonar B4: a function calling itself by name adds +1 flat per recursive call site. Implementation: track the current function name on the stack alongside the running total (Vec<(String, u32)>). In visit_call_expression, if callee is an Identifier whose name matches the top of the function-name stack, self.flat(). Skip method calls (e.g. this.foo()) at v1 — pure name match only. Fixture: a recursive fibonacci that gets +1 for each direct self-call.

title: Refactor.DuplicateBlock — token-mode opt-in scan

Slides a fixed-token window over the file's lexer output regardless of statement boundaries; canonicalises identifiers + literals; hashes; pushes into the same DUPLICATE_BLOCKS corpus slot, distinguished by a kind: TokenHash discriminator so finalize can dedupe overlap with AST hits. Useful for catching duplicates that span non-statement boundaries (e.g., a multi-line conditional broken across statements differently in two places).
close_reason: Implemented in f71e9ba. DuplicateBlock::with_tokens(N) opts in to a sliding-token-window pass alongside AST mode. title: [A4] Suppression directives (// cofferdam-disable-...)
description:
Engine-level suppression directives, Biome-style primary syntax with ESLint-style aliases for refugees.

PRIMARY SYNTAX (Biome-inspired):
- // cofferdam-ignore: <CheckId>: <reason>            (next-line, default)
- // cofferdam-ignore-start: <CheckId>                (range start)
- // cofferdam-ignore-end                             (range end)
- // cofferdam-ignore-file: <CheckId>                 (file-wide, must be at top)
- ID-omitted form: // cofferdam-ignore                (suppress all on next line, engine emits info: 'broad suppression')

ALIASES (accepted, normalized to primary by formatter):
- // cofferdam-disable-next-line <CheckId>
- // cofferdam-disable-line <CheckId>
- // cofferdam-disable-block <CheckId> ... // cofferdam-enable-block
- // cofferdam-disable-file

REASON FIELD POLICY:
- Default off (optional).
- Required for Warning category by default.
- Per-check override via OptionSpec.

WHY BIOME OVER ESLINT:
Biome did the suppression design after a decade of watching ESLint accrete confusion (line vs next-line, block vs line comments, no reason field). One canonical form + a reason expectation produces less wallpaper-suppression. ESLint-style aliases honour muscle memory for refugees without bloating the canonical surface.

PARSING LOCATION:
Engine pre-pass (single comment-scan), not per-check. Engine maintains a suppression map and filters the final issue list. Keeps checks simple, makes interactions auditable.

INTERACTION WITH BASELINE:
Suppressed findings do NOT enter the baseline. (Cleaner than the alternative — a baselined-AND-suppressed finding is an audit trap.)

OUT OF SCOPE:
- IDE/LSP code-action to insert a suppression directive (separate bead).
- Linting the suppression directives themselves (e.g., 'unused suppression' check) — separate bead, classic third-pass work.

Unblocks cd-zaf (docs).

title: [A5] Declarative file scoping
description:
Each check declares `files: { extensions, pathPattern, excludePatterns }` so engine skips inapplicable files cheaply (no parse, no run() call).

Replaces the `scannable?/1` boilerplate every rovikore check writes today.

```ts
files: {
  extensions: ["ts", "tsx"],
  pathPattern: "**/resources/**",
  excludePatterns: ["**/dev_checks/**"],
}
```

Engine evaluates these against discovery output before invoking run(). Per-check exclusions also overridable in cofferdam.toml.

title: [A6] ctx.report with fix payload
description:
`ctx.report({ message, span | line+column, fix? })` — the fix is an optional list of text edits that autofix consumes in phase 3.

```ts
ctx.report({
  message: "...",
  span: node.span,
  fix: ctx.replaceText(node.source.span, '"@org/http"'),
});
```

Helpers: `ctx.replaceText(span, str)`, `ctx.insertBefore(span, str)`, `ctx.insertAfter(span, str)`, `ctx.removeRange(span)`.

Out of scope here: the autofix interactive engine. This issue just lands the data shape on Issue + ctx helpers.

Acceptance:
- Issue includes optional `fix: TextEdit[]` after serialization
- Round-trips through napi without loss

title: [A7] TS plugin loader (napi worker_threads)
description:
Phase 4 deliverable. Each plugin module loads into its own worker_thread for crash containment + per-plugin timeout. Engine sends `Run` messages with serialized SourceFile + AST handle, gets back Issue[] over the wire.

Depends on the broader napi-rs FFI surface (already cd-napi epic territory in the existing plan).

Acceptance:
- A plugin file under .cofferdam/checks/ is auto-loaded
- Plugin throwing during run() is contained — that file emits a Warning.PluginCrashed and analysis continues
- Plugin run timeout enforced (default 5s; configurable)

title: Normalize path separators in output
description:
On Windows, output mixes forward and backslashes (e.g. `C:/Users/tajdi/rovikore-landing-page\worker-configuration.d.ts`) because the user-supplied root uses one and the walker emits the other.

Fix: normalize all displayed paths to forward slashes (cross-platform consistency, matches what most editors/CI tools expect for source links).

Acceptance:
- Output paths use `/` only
- File paths still resolve correctly when clicked in editors
- Span byte offsets unaffected

title: Readability.MaxFunctionLength AST check
description:
Hardcoded limit (50 logical lines). Config arrives in cd-9.

Measure on:
- FunctionDeclaration
- FunctionExpression
- ArrowFunctionExpression (when body is BlockStatement)
- MethodDefinition

Skip arrow bodies that are expressions (`x => x + 1`) — those are by definition short.

Length = end line - start line of the body block. Don't count comments? Punt that to a config option later.

Acceptance:
- 51-line function: one finding
- 50-line function: no finding
- Nested function: each measured independently
- base_priority: -5 (Readability)

title: Design.MaxParameters AST check
description:
Hardcoded limit (5 params). Cheap counter check — validates that base_priority on Check::meta is ergonomic for tunable thresholds.

Counts on FormalParameters node. Counts:
- Regular params
- Default-valued params (`x = 1`)
- Rest params (`...args` counts as 1)
- Destructured params (`{ a, b }` counts as 1, not 2)

Acceptance:
- 6-param function: one finding
- 5-param function: no finding
- Destructured: `function f({ a, b, c, d, e, f, g })` — one param, no finding
- base_priority: 5 (Design)

title: Refactor.DuplicateBlock — AST-subtree canonical hashing
description: Replace v1's source-text canonicalisation with proper AST-subtree hashing. Walk the AST, emitting node-kind tags + canonicalised identifier indices into the hasher, instead of regex-substituting the source string. More robust to whitespace + comment placement, distinguishes shape ambiguities the text version flattens (e.g., method call vs function call with same name). Big change; defer until token-mode + config land.
close_reason: Implemented in bb4d03b. AstHashWalker (impl Visit<'a>) emits structural tags + canonicalised identifier indices + literal values per AST node, replacing source-text canonicalise+hash_str. 153 tests pass (5 new). bestefforttools went 396→398 (+2 DuplicateBlock). Token mode unchanged. v1 doesn't tag TS-specific nodes — follow-up if needed.

title: Refactor.DuplicateBlock — Unicode identifier support
description: Today canonicalise() in refactor.rs walks UTF-8 bytes assuming ASCII identifiers. TS allows Unicode identifiers (e.g., greek letters, Han characters). Switch to walking by char_indices() and recognising Unicode XID_Start / XID_Continue. Edge case but worth fixing before declaring DuplicateBlock 'production-grade'.
close_reason: Implemented in ec6534c. Unicode-ident is_xid_{start,continue} replaces ASCII-only byte scan in canonicalise() and tokenise(). 2 new tests pass; 148 total. bestefforttools regression-free at 396 findings.

title: Per-slot locking for CorpusIndex (parallel-engine prereq)
description: Today CorpusIndex serialises all slot access through a single Mutex. Fine for the sequential per-file loop. When per-file parallelism lands, swap the slot value type so locks become per-slot (e.g. inner type becomes Box<dyn AnySlot + Send>, where AnySlot wraps Mutex<Box<dyn Any + Send>>). Public API (CorpusKey + with_slot) stays the same.

title: Switch zig setup action to mlugg/setup-zig
description:
release.yml uses korandoru/setup-zig@v1. mlugg/setup-zig is the more actively maintained alternative — most modern Rust+Zig CI pipelines have moved to it. Same API, different repo.
